headline: Committee hears testimony on license plate reader, facial recognition bills

meeting.body: Maui County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee
meeting.voteItem: Taking up DRIP 27 and DRIP 26 together
meeting.summary: The committee heard police, prosecutors and the public on Bills 112 and 113 on facial recognition and license plate readers, then recessed until tomorrow.
meeting.recap: The committee took up Bill 113, on license plate reader data, and Bill 112, on facial recognition, together.[[0:06:01]] Bill 113 would ban selling or commercial use of automated license plate reader data.[[0:06:54]] A police lieutenant said the police department does not currently have facial recognition technology.[[0:10:16]] The lieutenant said license plate readers record a plate, image, time and location but do not identify people.[[0:12:39]] The prosecuting attorney's office cautioned against limiting what courts may count as probable cause or reasonable suspicion.[[0:24:34]] The managing director said the county has no contracts with Flock camera companies, to the county's knowledge.[[0:32:00]] Another testifier asked for a 30-day limit on keeping camera data.[[1:58:55]] A Lahaina resident said cameras helped the community recover from thefts.[[2:08:58]] Members agreed to close spoken testimony and keep written testimony open.[[2:15:21]] Staff will send a letter asking the state about license plate reader cameras in Maui County.[[2:24:28]] The committee recessed until 9 a.m. tomorrow.[[2:32:45]]
decided: With no objections, the committee took up both items together.
The committee took a 10-minute break during public testimony.
With no objections, spoken testimony was closed and written testimony stays open.
With no objections, the meeting was put in recess until 9 a.m. tomorrow.
meeting.next: The prosecuting attorney's office was asked to write specific amendment language for the committee to consider tomorrow. The police will send a letter with line items, costs and any agreements for the license plate reader cameras. Staff will send a letter to the state asking about license plate reader cameras in Maui County and where they are. The managing director will follow up with the name of the company behind state law enforcement cameras that he said are not Flock cameras.
